analysis.investment_thesis: Prism Johnson fails both legs of the Magic Formula catastrophically — an Earnings Yield of ~0.35% (EBIT ≈ INR 26 Cr on a INR 7,393 Cr EV) and ROCE of just 2.22% make it uninvestable by any quantitative value screen. This is a capital-heavy, low-margin building materials business destroying shareholder value at current prices.
key_strengths: Consistent OCF generation (5/5 years positive, INR 737 Cr in FY25) — high depreciation masks EBITDA-to-cash conversion
Debt declining: borrowings fell from INR 2,425 Cr (FY20) to INR 1,694 Cr (FY25), D/E improving
Strong promoter holding (74.87%) and established multi-brand portfolio (Johnson Tiles, Champion Cement) with some pricing power
key_risks: Near-zero EBIT (~INR 26 Cr, 0.35% margin) leaves virtually no buffer — any cost spike turns the business loss-making
Earnings quality is poor: INR 293 Cr 'Other Income' in FY25 is the only reason PAT is positive; strip it out and the company loses money
EBITDA in structural decline: peaked at INR 922 Cr (FY21), collapsed to INR 472 Cr (FY25), 9Y CAGR of -1.4%
red_flags: P/E of 862x — effectively a zero-earnings company priced as a going concern
ROE of -4%: equity is being destroyed, not compounded
Other Income (INR 293 Cr) now exceeds EBIT (~INR 26 Cr) — operating business is economically non-viable at this scale
Finance costs of INR 230 Cr nearly equal total EBIT, making the business highly interest-rate sensitive
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Applying the Magic Formula, Prism Johnson scores at the very bottom on both required axes. Earnings Yield = EBIT/EV ≈ 26/7,393 = 0.35% — the threshold for "attractive" is 12%+. Return on Capital (ROCE as provided) = 2.22% against a required hurdle of 20%+. The company is essentially a large fixed-asset base (INR 7,302 Cr total assets) generating almost no operating profit after depreciation. The gross margin of 43.29% looks decent in isolation, but enormous depreciation (implied ~INR 446 Cr to bridge EBITDA of 472 Cr down to ~26 Cr EBIT) and finance costs of INR 230 Cr consume all operating economics. Revenue growth of just 3.8% CAGR over 9 years doesn't compensate.

The one redeeming feature is free cash flow (INR 526 Cr in FY25), but this is a product of high non-cash charges rather than genuine earnings power — and it's being used primarily to service debt and capex rather than compound capital. With a forward P/E still at 150x, the market is pricing in a turnaround that the fundamental trajectory — contracting EBITDA, near-zero EBIT, declining operating margins — does not support. By Magic Formula standards, there is no scenario where this stock ranks in the top two deciles on either earnings yield or ROIC. Avoid entirely.
